current_work: Investigating uncertainty calibration under noisy target prevalence estimates
Running targeted diagnostics on the first pilot result
Maintaining research code and experiment infrastructure
Developing a focused research question for a potential follow-up study
priorities: Determine whether the class-level pattern from the first pilot is stable
Keep the diagnostic tied to the original pilot rather than expanding the experiment matrix
Separate evidence about class-conditional behavior from speculation about mechanism
Decide whether the pilot warrants a second, controlled run

circumstances: The researcher runs the targeted class-level diagnostic planned on Day 24. The diagnostic shows that the apparent class-level divergence is strongest for one minority class and is much smaller for the others. A second seed is run only after the initial diagnostic suggests the pattern may matter; the second seed reproduces the direction but with a smaller effect. The researcher checks whether class imbalance alone explains the result and finds that it does not fully account for it. Rather than claiming a mechanism, they write a cautious interpretation and revise the pilot question toward robustness across class prevalence regimes. They also briefly inspect a related paper and update the experiment plan. No new dataset is introduced.

activities.title: Run the class-conditional diagnostic
activities.summary: The researcher prepared and ran the targeted class-level diagnostic on the first pilot output. The strongest divergence appeared for one low-frequency class, while other classes showed smaller changes.
activities.context: Follow-up explicitly planned after the non-monotonic aggregate result on Day 24.

activities.title: Check whether the class-level pattern is stable
activities.summary: Because the diagnostic concentrated the effect in one low-frequency class, the researcher ran one additional seed and compared aggregate and class-level results. The direction persisted but the magnitude was smaller.
activities.context: Additional seed was used only after the targeted diagnostic produced a specific pattern worth checking.

activities.title: Test a simple explanation for the class-level effect
activities.summary: The researcher reviewed related work on imbalanced-class calibration and compared class frequencies with observed calibration changes. Class imbalance appeared relevant but did not fully explain the observed pattern.
activities.context: Interpretation of the repeated class-level effect.

activities.title: Reframe the research question and constrain the next design
activities.summary: The researcher reframed the question toward robustness across prevalence regimes, preserved class-conditional reporting in the analysis plan, briefly checked benchmark references, removed unnecessary benchmark expansion, and wrote cautious interpretation and decision criteria.
activities.context: Transition from exploratory pilot result to a more focused research question.

key_observations: The class-level diagnostic showed that the largest calibration change is concentrated in one low-frequency class rather than uniformly across classes.
A second seed reproduced the direction of the effect, although the magnitude was smaller, making the pattern more credible but still preliminary.
Class imbalance alone does not fully account for the observed behavior, so the mechanism remains unresolved.
The researcher appropriately avoided claiming causality and reframed the question toward robustness across prevalence regimes.
The experiment scope remained bounded to the existing dataset and targeted diagnostics.
priority_alignment: The day directly addressed the most important uncertainty from the first pilot.
The second seed was added only to test stability of a specific observed pattern.
The researcher resisted broad benchmark expansion and preserved class-conditional reporting as part of the evaluation.
important_uncertainty: The class-specific effect may still depend on the selected dataset and seed.
The relationship between prevalence-estimation noise, class frequency, and calibration is not yet mechanistically established.
It remains unclear whether the revised robustness question is sufficiently novel for a larger study.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Compare the observed class-conditional behavior with a small set of closely related calibration methods and decide whether the pattern survives a method-level comparison before expanding the dataset or experiment matrix.

primary_action.title: Validate the revised research question
primary_action.reason: The pilot now has a repeatable directional signal, but the mechanism and generality are uncertain. A small method-level comparison can establish whether the observation is specific to the current method before broader expansion.

secondary_action.title: Keep the dataset fixed for now
secondary_action.reason: The current evidence does not yet justify a broader benchmark. Preserving the existing dataset makes the next comparison easier to interpret.

things_not_to_do: Do not claim that class imbalance causes the observed calibration effect.
Do not add multiple datasets before checking whether the effect appears across methods.
Do not expand the noise model or prevalence regimes yet.
Do not turn the exploratory pilot into a full paper project before the revised question is validated.
